chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'A man should not turn away from his clan, even if he possesses wealth and children, nor from their affection, their honor, and their defense with their hands and tongues. They are the people most vigilant for him from behind, most compassionate towards him, and most attentive to his needs if a calamity befalls him or some difficulties of affairs descend upon him.'
And whoever withholds his hand from his clan, he only withholds one hand from them, but many hands will be withheld from him.
And whoever softens his inner circle, his friend will recognize affection from him.
And whoever extends his hand with goodness when he finds the opportunity, Allah will replace for him what he spent in his world, and multiply for him in his Hereafter.
And a truthful tongue for a person, Allah makes it among the people better than the wealth he consumes and inherits.
Let not one of you increase in arrogance and greatness in his own soul, and distance himself from his clan, if he is affluent in wealth.
And let not one of you increase in asceticism towards his brother, nor distance himself from him, if he does not see magnanimity from him, and he is needy in wealth.
And let not one of you be oblivious to kinship; with it is the need, if one were to cover it with what does not benefit him if he withholds it, nor harm him if he consumes it.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and social benefits of maintaining kinship ties according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali (peace be upon him) that a person should maintain strong ties with their clan, regardless of wealth, as they provide defense and support. The hadith emphasizes that withholding kindness from family results in losing support, while extending generosity is rewarded by Allah in this world and the next. It also warns against arrogance due to wealth or asceticism due to poverty, urging believers to remain connected to their relatives.
